title: Shagwong Point, Hill, and Reef
summary: Shagwong is a Montauk placename for a hill, point of land, and reef on the northeastern part of the peninsula, within the Indian Fields area.
history_content: The name remains attached to Shagwong Point and Shagwong Reef on the north side of Montauk. A later map spelling, Shewango, appears to refer to the same place-name tradition.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Shagwong, Shagwannock, Shawango, and Shewango. Shawango and Shewango are treated as map or spelling errors connected with Shagwong rather than as separate places. The secure meaning remains unresolved.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are powerful; they embody histories and can “claim” ownership over the spaces we inhabit.”

— Kaleigh Bradley, What’s in a Name? Place Names, History, and Colonialism (2015), Article opening
preservation_content: Shagwong links present-day Montauk coastal geography with an older Native place-name for land and water features around the northeastern shore.
